You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 659a37844abc00c3dc676bb1faed29c1dacbf59f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2021 09:40:27 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: bsg-lib: Fix commands without data transfer in
 bsg_transport_sg_io_fn()

Set ret to 0 after the initial permission checks to avoid leaking -EPERM
for commands without data transfer.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210731074027.1185545-3-hch@lst.de
Fixes: 75ca56409e5b ("scsi: bsg: Move the whole request execution into the SCSI/transport handlers")
Signed-off-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
---
 block/bsg-lib.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/block/bsg-lib.c b/block/bsg-lib.c
index 239ebf747141..ccb98276c964 100644
--- a/block/bsg-lib.c
+++ b/block/bsg-lib.c
@@ -72,6 +72,7 @@ static int bsg_transport_sg_io_fn(struct request_queue *q, struct sg_io_v4 *hdr,
 		job->bidi_bio = NULL;
 	}
 
+	ret = 0;
 	if (hdr->dout_xfer_len) {
 		ret = blk_rq_map_user(rq->q, rq, NULL, uptr64(hdr->dout_xferp),
 				hdr->dout_xfer_len, GFP_KERNEL);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the function `bsg_transport_sg_io_fn()` returning an error code `-EPERM` (indicating a permission error) for commands that did not involve any data transfer. This occurred because the return value `ret` was not reset to 0 after the initial permission checks, leading to incorrect error reporting for valid commands that did not require data transfer. The patch fixes this by explicitly setting `ret` to 0 before checking for data transfer, ensuring that valid commands are processed correctly without leaking the permission error.

This occurred because the return value `ret` was not reset to 0 after the initial permission checks, leading to incorrect error reporting for valid commands that did not require data transfer. The patch fixes this by explicitly setting `ret` to 0 before checking for data transfer, ensuring that valid commands are processed correctly without leaking the permission error.
